prompt:
A full-fidelity desktop website homepage design comp, landscape, shown flat with no browser frame and no device. This is the website of Beauty From Ashes Surgical Ministry, a Christian nonprofit in the Carolinas that provides reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost. Visual world (keep exactly): the page ground is a pale buff-grey salt-glazed stoneware surface with a fine orange-peel texture; headlines in a deep iron-brown dignified serif; small spaced-capital eyebrows; body text in a clean humanist sans; every clickable action is solid cobalt blue with a subtly hand-brushed edge; dividers are thin hand-brushed cobalt lines; amber and olive-green wood-ash glaze appears only in the photography. Layout, top to bottom, centered composition:

1. NAVIGATION BAR (thin, full width): at left a text wordmark "Beauty From Ashes" in the serif with "SURGICAL MINISTRY" in small spaced capitals below; centered links "Our Mission", "How We Help", "Stories", "Get Involved", "Contact"; at right a small "EN | ES" switch and a solid cobalt button "Give".

2. CENTERED HERO TEXT (about 35% of the height): eyebrow "A CHRISTIAN SURGICAL MINISTRY · CHARLOTTE & FORT MILL" centered; a large centered iron-brown serif headline "Restoring more than what can be seen."; a centered paragraph "Reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost, for children and adults whose need exceeds their means. Open to everyone."; two centered buttons side by side: solid cobalt "Ask for help" and iron-brown outlined "Refer someone".

3. THE SHELF (lower 55%): a wide, quiet photograph of a long weathered wooden shelf against a plain warm stone-colored wall, holding six different hand-thrown Carolina stoneware vessels evenly spaced, each a different shape and size (a tall jug, a round jar, a wide bowl, a slender bottle, a pitcher, a small cup) and each glazed differently (amber ash runs, olive-green ash glaze, cobalt brushwork on grey salt glaze, iron-brown, speckled buff, deep blue), so no two are alike. Directly beneath each vessel, on the stoneware ground below the photograph, its label in a column: a serif heading and one line of small sans text: "We Listen." / "We give every patient the time their story deserves." — "We Protect." / "We hold patient safety as our highest surgical standard." — "We Pray." / "We pray with every patient who welcomes it." — "We Accompany." / "We walk with every patient long after surgery ends." — "We Honor." / "We honor the sacrifice behind every patient's decision." — "We Serve." / "We extend surgical care where need exceeds means."

Overall: calm, dignified, professional, warm and hopeful; unmistakably a real nonprofit website with crisp, legible web typography. Not a church bulletin, not a cosmetic surgery advertisement, not a rustic boutique.
